nodes.summary: Every element of the set $T_0$ of reals $n / 3^k$, where $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers, $n$ is stable and $\lVert n \rVert = 3k + 2$ (with $\lVert n \rVert$ the integer complexity of $n$), is a nonnegative real number.
nodes.title: The set $T_0$ is nonnegative

nodes.summary: Write $\lVert n \rVert$ for the integer complexity of a natural number $n$, and call $n$ stable when $n > 0$ and $\lVert 3^k n \rVert = \lVert n \rVert + 3k$ for every natural number $k$. The set $T_0 \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ consists of the reals $n / 3^k$, where $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers, $n$ is stable and $\lVert n \rVert = 3k + 2$.
nodes.title: The set $T_0$ built from stable numbers

nodes.summary: Let $T_0$ be the set of reals $n / 3^k$, where $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers, $n$ is stable and $\lVert n \rVert = 3k + 2$ (with $\lVert n \rVert$ the integer complexity of $n$), and let $K$ be the closure of $T_0$ in $\mathbb{R}$. nodes.title: The closure of $T_0$ is an arithmetical compact set (Theorem 2)

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be an arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$. For every natural number $n$, the $n$-th derived set $K^{(n)}$ of $K$ (the set of accumulation points, iterated $n$ times, so that $K^{(0)} = K$) is an arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$.
nodes.title: Derived sets of an arithmetical compact set are arithmetical (Proposition 7)

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and let $\mu$ and $\rho$ be natural numbers. For each natural number $j$ let $K^{(j)}$ be the $j$-th iterated derived set (the set of accumulation points, iterated $j$ times) of $K$ and $T_j = K^{(j)} \setminus K^{(j+1)}$ its $j$-th layer, and for a natural number $m$ let $\lVert m \rVert_K$ be the stability gauge of $K$ with module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$ at $m$. Then $K$ is an…
nodes.title: Arithmetical compact sets

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is stable when $n > 0$ and $\lVert 3^k n \rVert = \lVert n \rVert + 3k$ for every natural number $k$, where $\lVert m \rVert$ is the integer complexity of $m$.
nodes.title: Stable numbers for integer complexity

nodes.summary: If $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is an arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$, then $K$ is a quasi-arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$.
nodes.title: Arithmetical compact sets are quasi-arithmetical

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a quasi-arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$. For each natural number $j$ let $K^{(j)}$ be the $j$-th iterated derived set of $K$ and $T_j = K^{(j)} \setminus K^{(j+1)}$ its $j$-th layer. If $n, \ell, u, \ell', u'$ are natural numbers with $n / \rho^\ell \in T_u$ and $\rho n / \rho^{\ell'} \in T_{u'}$, then $\ell' \mu - u' = \ell \mu - u + \mu$ as integers.
nodes.title: Multiplying by the ratio raises the gauge index by the module (Proposition 6)

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a quasi-arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$. For each natural number $j$ let $K^{(j)}$ be the $j$-th iterated derived set of $K$ and $T_j = K^{(j)} \setminus K^{(j+1)}$ its $j$-th layer. If $n, p, q, v, w$ are natural numbers with $n / \rho^p \in T_v$ and $n / \rho^q \in T_w$, then $p \mu - v = q \mu - w$ as integers.
nodes.title: The layer index of a quasi-arithmetical compact set is well defined (Proposition 5)

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and let $\mu$ and $\rho$ be natural numbers. Then $K$ is a quasi-arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$ when $\rho \ge 2$, $K$ is a self-similar compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$, and there is a function $\kappa : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $K \setminus \{0\} = \{n / \rho^k : n, k \in \mathbb{N},\ \rho \nmid n,\ k \ge \kappa(n)\}$.
nodes.title: Quasi-arithmetical compact sets

nodes.summary: If $K$ is a quasi-arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and natural-number ratio $\rho$, then $K$ is a self-similar compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$.
nodes.title: Quasi-arithmetical compact sets are self-similar

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a self-similar compact set of module $\mu \ge 1$ and ratio $\rho$. Then there is a strictly decreasing map $\alpha \mapsto K[\alpha]$ from the ordinals $\alpha \le \omega^\omega$ onto $K$ (so $K$ has order type $\omega^\omega + 1$ under the reverse order) with $K[\omega^\omega] = 0$, $K[0] > 0$ and $K \subseteq [0, K[0]]$.

Then…

Let $\alpha \mapsto K[\alpha]$ be a strictly decreasing map from the ordinals $\alpha \le \omega^\omega$ onto $K$, and $\alpha \mapsto T_0[\alpha]$ a strictly decreasing map from the ordinals $\alpha < \omega^\omega$ onto $T_0$. Then for…

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a natural number and $\rho$ a real number. A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a self-similar compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$ when $\rho > 1$, $K$ is nonempty and compact, $K \subseteq [0, \infty)$, $K$ is well ordered by the reverse order $x \preceq y \iff x \ge y$ (every nonempty subset of $K$ has a largest element), and $\rho K^{(\mu)} = K$, where $K^{(\mu)}$ is the $\mu$-th derived set…
nodes.title: Self-similar compact set

nodes.summary: For a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and $u \ge 0$, write $T_u(A) = A^{(u)} \setminus A^{(u+1)}$ for the $u$-th layer of $A$, where $A^{(u)}$ is the $u$-th derived set of $A$. Then for every set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and every $u \ge 0$, $T_{u+1}(K) = T_u(K')$, where $K'$ is the derived set of $K$.
nodes.title: Layers of the derived set

nodes.summary: For every set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, the layer $T_0$ of $K$ equals $K \setminus K'$, where $K'$ is the derived set of $K$ (its set of accumulation points); that is, $T_0$ is the set of isolated points of $K$.
nodes.title: The zeroth layer is the set of isolated points

nodes.summary: For a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and a natural number $u$, let $K^{(u)}$ be the $u$-th derived set of $K$ (the derived set, i.e. the set of accumulation points, iterated $u$ times, with $K^{(0)} = K$). The layer of $K$ of index $u$ is $T_u = K^{(u)} \setminus K^{(u+1)}$, the set of points of $K^{(u)}$ that are isolated in $K^{(u)}$.
nodes.title: Layers of the iterated derived sets

nodes.summary: If $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a self-similar compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$, then $\rho K^{(\mu)} = K$, where $K^{(\mu)}$ is the $\mu$-th derived set of $K$ (the set of accumulation points, iterated $\mu$ times) and $\rho K^{(\mu)}$ is its image under multiplication by $\rho$.
nodes.title: Self-similarity equation

Let $\ell$ be the least natural number such that $n / \rho^\ell$ lies in some layer $T_u$ (division by $0$ gives $0$), and let $u$ be the least index with $n / \rho^\ell \in T_u$. nodes.title: Un-normalized stability gauge

nodes.summary: For every set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and all natural numbers $\mu$ and $\rho$, the stability gauge $n \mapsto \lVert n \rVert_K$ of $K$ with module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$ takes the value $0$ at $n = 1$, that is, $\lVert 1 \rVert_K = 0$.
nodes.title: The stability gauge vanishes at one

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $\mu$ and $\rho$ be natural numbers, and for a natural number $n$ let $g(n)$ be the un-normalized stability gauge of $n$ for $K$, $\mu$ and $\rho$: the integer $\ell \mu - u$, where $\ell$ is least such that $n / \rho^\ell$ lies in some layer $T_u$ of $K$ and $u$ is the least such index (and $g(n) = 0$ if there is no such $\ell$). The stability gauge of $n$ is the integer…
nodes.title: Stability gauge

nodes.summary: If $n$ is a stable natural number, then its stable complexity equals its integer complexity: $\lVert n \rVert_{\mathrm{st}} = \lVert n \rVert$.
nodes.title: Stable complexity of a stable number

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $\lVert m \rVert$ denote the integer complexity of a positive integer $m$, with $\lVert 0 \rVert = 0$, and let $a$ be the least natural number such that $3^a n$ is stable, with $a = 0$ if there is none. The stable complexity of $n$ is the integer $\lVert n \rVert_{\mathrm{st}} = \lVert 3^a n \rVert - 3a$.
nodes.title: Stable complexity

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
